summary: The Romanian Government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education, offers scholarships each year to citizens of non-EU countries to study at accredited Romanian higher education institutions, under Government Decision no. 288/1993. The 2026-2027 call covers bachelor's, master's and PhD studies in all fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy. Bachelor's and master's courses are taught only in Romanian, so students who do not speak Romanian first take a preparatory Romanian-language year. The award finances tuition, a monthly scholarship and dormitory accommodation (within a subsidy and subject to places) for one study cycle.
eligibility_notes:
Open to foreign citizens of all non-EU countries. Not eligible: citizens of Romanian origin or members of Romanian historical communities near Romania (they have separate programmes); people who have requested or hold protection in Romania; recognised stateless persons residing in Romania; members of the diplomatic and consular corps accredited to Romania and their family members; administrative and technical staff of accredited diplomatic missions and consular offices; staff of international organisations based in Romania and their family members; and current holders of a Romanian state scholarship for the same study cycle.

Applicants need good results: an average of at least 7 on the Romanian scale, or a 'Good' score where that applies, for the last school they graduated from. They must submit a complete file, with study documents issued by institutions that are accredited or recognised in the issuing country, and meet the enrolment deadline. A valid passport is required; without one you cannot apply. Applications that do not meet the conditions may be treated as ineligible.

Bachelor's applicants hold a baccalaureate or equivalent. Master's applicants hold a bachelor's degree. PhD applicants hold a master's or equivalent, must obtain a written agreement from a doctoral tutor who belongs to the doctoral school before applying, and must pass an admission interview.

Language: bachelor's and master's holders study only in Romanian. PhD holders may study in Romanian or in a foreign language set by the doctoral school. Applicants who do not speak Romanian get a preparatory year first, except PhD holders studying in a foreign language. You are exempt from the preparatory year if you hold Romanian study documents or have at least three consecutive years of study in Romanian within the Romanian national system, pass the Romanian language test needed for university enrolment, or hold a Romanian language certificate at level B1 or above.

There is no age limit. Candidates who are under 18 when the course starts need notarised parental consent. Each year's applications are judged separately; a previous application does not affect this year's. Only one application is allowed per programme.
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated. Applicants under 18 at the course start need notarised parental consent (with translation if needed). No work experience is required for bachelor's or master's; PhD applicants need a doctoral tutor's written agreement and a letter of intent listing publications and a research project.
funding_summary: The award finances: tuition for the Romanian preparatory year (where it applies) and for the main studies, up to the length of one university cycle; a monthly scholarship during the preparatory year and during bachelor's, master's or PhD studies, up to one cycle; and dormitory accommodation costs within the Ministry of Education subsidy, subject to available places. Application, Romanian language test, doctoral admission contest and aptitude test fees are waived. The monthly amount is set by Government decision and paid in Romanian lei; no figure is given on the pages read. International travel and personal expenses are not covered.
programmes_note: All fields are open except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy, which get no scholarships. The scholarship pages do not give a fixed list of programmes; applicants choose a programme and domain on the application form. Bachelor's and master's applicants can only choose programmes taught in Romanian. The Study in Romania programme search filters by degree (bachelor's, master's, doctoral, preparatory year), language, city and about 120 study domains, including: Accounting; Administrative sciences; Aerospace engineering; Agronomy; Applied Modern Languages; Architecture; Automotive Engineering; Biochemistry; Biology; Biotechnologies; Business administration; Business Information Systems; Chemical Engineering; Chemistry; Civil Engineering; Communication Sciences; Computer Science Computers and Information Technology; Cultural Studies; Economics; Educational Sciences; Electrical Engineering; Electronic Engineering, Telecommunications and Informational Technologies; Environmental Engineering; Finance; Food Engineering; Geography; Geology; History; Horticulture; Industrial Engineering; International Relations and European Studies; Law; Management; Marketing; Mathematics; Mechanical Engineering; Music; Philosophy; Physics; Political Sciences; Psychology; Sociology; Theatre and Performing Arts; Veterinary Medicine; Visual Arts; and others. The same filter also lists Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy, which are not covered by this scholarship.
institutions_note: Accredited higher education institutions in Romania. The Study in Romania site lists 51 institutions in 20 cities (Alba Iulia, Arad, Bacau, Brasov, Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Constanta, Craiova, Galati, Iasi, Oradea, Petrosani, Pitesti, Ploiesti, Sibiu, Suceava, Targoviste, Targu Jiu, Targu Mures, Timisoara). Those readable include the National University of Physical Education and Sports of Bucharest, SNSPA Bucharest, 1 Decembrie 1918 University of Alba Iulia, Aurel Vlaicu University of Arad, Vasile Alecsandri University of Bacau, Transilvania University of Brasov, Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Babes-Bolyai University Cluj-Napoca, Ovidius University of Constanta, University of Craiova, Dunarea de Jos University of Galati, Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iasi and Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi. The pages do not say which of them take scholarship holders. The applicant picks the programme and university on the form; if the chosen university cannot be honoured, the Ministry of Education may offer another in the same field, depending on availability. Later requests to change field or university are not considered.

summary.detail: For graduates of high school or pre-university studies who hold a baccalaureate or equivalent, and for those applying for further university study. Lasts 3 to 6 years depending on the specialisation and ends with a bachelor's exam. Taught only in Romanian; non-Romanian speakers start with a preparatory Romanian-language year. All fields open except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy.

For holders of a bachelor's degree. Lasts 1, 1.5 or 2 years and ends with a dissertation exam. Taught only in Romanian; non-Romanian speakers start with a preparatory Romanian-language year. All fields open except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy.

For graduate students or equivalent. Lasts 4 years and ends with presentation of a PhD thesis. Taught in Romanian or in a foreign language set by the doctoral school; a holder studying in a foreign language does not take the preparatory year. Before applying you need a doctoral tutor's written agreement, and you must pass an admission interview. Application needs a letter of intent and a detailed research project description. All fields open except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy.

benefits.limit_text: Exemption from registration and other fees for processing the application, the Romanian language test, the doctoral admission contest and specific aptitude tests
Tuition for the Romanian preparatory year, and for the main studies up to the duration of one university cycle
benefits.conditions: One cycle only (bachelor's, master's or PhD). The scholarship cannot be deferred or moved to the next academic year.

benefits.limit_text: Monthly scholarship during the preparatory year and during bachelor's, master's or doctoral studies, up to one cycle; the number and amount are set by Government decision and paid in Romanian lei (amount not stated on the pages read)
benefits.conditions: Lost or suspended if the student misses the minimum attendance, does not earn the minimum ECTS credits, is expelled, changes field of study, breaches the university contract or regulations, or asks in writing to give it up. Loss for missing attendance or credits can be reversed only if the student meets those requirements the next academic year and total scholarship years do not exceed the cycle length; the other losses cannot be reversed.

benefits.limit_text: Dormitory accommodation costs financed within the Ministry of Education subsidy, subject to available places
benefits.conditions: Holders must contact the host university about accommodation conditions. The general scholarships page says dormitory accommodation is the student's own responsibility; the 2026 methodology and FAQ list it as a benefit within the subsidy. Confirm with the university.
Stated on the general state scholarships page.

benefits.limit_text: Personal expenses and the cost of the visa application steps are not covered
benefits.conditions: The holder must complete the visa application steps and bear all related costs.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance is not mentioned as a benefit
benefits.conditions: At enrolment a medical certificate of fitness for study and freedom from contagious diseases is required.

requirements.text: Copies of diplomas: baccalaureate or equivalent, plus bachelor's, master's or doctorate where applicable. Authorised translations into English, French, Spanish or Romanian where applicable. Study documents must be apostilled under the Hague Convention or authenticated by the relevant home-country authorities (for example the education ministry).
Copies of transcripts of completed studies, with authorised translations where applicable (same apostille or authentication rule).
Copy of the birth certificate or equivalent, with authorised translation where applicable.
Copy of the first three pages of a valid passport. You cannot apply without a valid passport.
CV in English, French or Romanian.
Letter of intent in English, French or Romanian listing scientific works and publications, a detailed description of the research project, and the doctoral tutor's written agreement.
Proof of name change, with translation if needed.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if your name differs between documents

requirements.text: Certificate of passing the baccalaureate, bachelor's or master's exam, for graduates who do not yet hold the diploma, with translation if needed.
Certificate of completing the Romanian preparatory year, or a Romanian language competence certificate (B1 or above), if you claim an exemption from the preparatory year.
Notarised parental consent, with translation if needed.
requirements.conditional_rule: Candidates under 18 on the course start date

requirements.text: Each document scanned separately from the original as a PDF. Registration is valid only if you sign the GDPR declaration consenting to personal data processing. Documents cannot be added or edited after submission.

application_steps.title: Check the rules and prepare apostilled documents
application_steps.detail: Confirm you are a non-EU citizen not in an excluded group, have an average of at least 7 (or 'Good'), and have a valid passport. Prepare diplomas, transcripts, birth certificate, passport copy and CV, with translations and an apostille or authentication. PhD applicants first get the doctoral tutor's written agreement and write a letter of intent and research project.

application_steps.title: Create an account on the scholarships platform
application_steps.detail: Applications are accepted only through the Study in Romania scholarships platform, available in English and French. Applications sent to ministry offices, ministry staff emails, Romanian embassies or foreign embassies in Bucharest are not considered.

application_steps.title: Complete the online form and upload every document
application_steps.detail: The form covers personal details, contact information, academic background and preferred study domains, plus document uploads. Choose a programme taught in Romanian for bachelor's or master's. Only one application per programme. The 2026-2027 window ran from 16 February to 31 March 2026. Incomplete applications are not considered and documents cannot be added or edited after submission.

application_steps.title: Sign the GDPR declaration and keep the confirmation
application_steps.detail: Registration is valid only with the signed GDPR declaration. After submitting you see a confirmation message on the platform and receive a confirmation email.

application_steps.title: Competition of files by the two ministries
application_steps.detail: Awards are made through a competition of files run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education. The pages name these conditions: complete file, study documents from accredited institutions, the grade average, and following the submission methodology. PhD candidates must also pass an admission interview. Scoring weights and the number of awards are not stated.

application_steps.title: Results by email around 15 July
application_steps.detail: For the 2026-2027 call, results were sent by email to all applicants around 15 July 2026, to the address registered on the platform.

application_steps.title: Receive the letter of acceptance and answer on the platform
application_steps.detail: The Ministry of Education issues a letter of acceptance for studies in Romania that names the host university (or universities) and any preparatory-year obligation. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs sends the original to the university and a scan can be downloaded. Within the stated time you accept or decline electronically; if you decline, do so quickly so another candidate can be chosen. The scholarship cannot be deferred.

application_steps.title: Apply for the long-stay study visa
application_steps.detail: Accepting candidates request the long-stay study visa, where a visa is needed, using the acceptance letter. All visa costs are the holder's. Family members' travel conditions are checked with the Romanian immigration authority.

application_steps.title: Contact the university and enrol
application_steps.detail: During the university's enrolment period, report to the International Relations Office or Rector's Office with the complete original application file, a copy of the acceptance letter, passport (original and copy) with a valid long-stay visa or residence permit, a medical certificate, and any other documents the university requires, possibly with authenticated copies and Romanian translations. The academic year usually starts on 1 October, but each university sets its own calendar. The university may also ask for aptitude tests.

application_steps.title: Keep your scholarship during the study cycle
application_steps.detail: Follow Romanian law, the institution's rules and the methodology. The scholarship ends if you lose student status, and is lost for missing attendance or ECTS credits, expulsion, changing field, breaching the study contract or asking in writing. Loss for attendance or credits may be reversed the next year if requirements are met and total years stay within the cycle length.

not_stated: The monthly scholarship amount in lei (only that it is set by Government decision)
Number of scholarships available in the 2026-2027 call (an embassy page of the foreign ministry reportedly gives a figure, but it could not be opened)
Selection criteria beyond a complete file, the grade average and the PhD interview; how files are scored
Which universities and programmes take scholarship holders (no fixed list on the scholarship pages)

Return or reporting obligations after graduation
fetch_problems: mae.ro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs main site and several embassy sub-sites) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt, so the ministry's own notice and any quota figure could not be read.
The Study in Romania universities page shows 51 institutions in 3 pages, but only the first 20 could be read.
The Study in Romania FAQ page and landing page contain no scholarship details; the scholarship platform pages were used instead.
notes: Sources disagree on the preparatory-year exemption: the methodology, FAQ and 2026-2027 call say three consecutive years of study in Romanian within the Romanian system; the general scholarships page says four.

Sources disagree on accommodation: the general state scholarships page says dormitory accommodation is the student's responsibility, while the methodology and FAQ list dormitory costs as financed within a subsidy, subject to places.
The scholarship-about page carries a '2025' title but states the 2026 calendar (16 February to 31 March 2026, results around 15 July 2026).
The 2026-2027 application window has closed; the 'intake' for this cycle is the 2026-2027 academic year. Dates are loaded elsewhere.
The preparatory Romanian-language year is part of the award for non-Romanian speakers but is not itself a degree level.
Carried over from stored data (not re-read as a separate page): stored note that the number and amount of scholarships are set by Government decision, which matches the general scholarships page.
